newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while feeder cattle were called steady to 0.200 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Mixed market factors were cited in live cattle futures with higher choice beef values supportive but the $68 per cwt live sales Tuesday considered disappointing due to expectations earlier in the week that cash markets would trade at $69, analysts said.
April's situation at a premium to cash cattle prices ahead of its expiration at noon may pressure that month but June may find support on its discount to cash, they said.
April closed at 69.325 cents a lb Tuesday versus the $68.00 per cwt cash cattle sales.
Cash cattle prices usually decline seasonally from April to June but that anticipated break in prices is already in the market in June futures, which Tuesday closed at 64.675 cents.

Feeder cattle futures were expected to show further support after posting new contract highs in April and August Tuesday. Cash feeder cattle markets remain strong and the latest CME feeder cattle index rose further. Calls for easier corn futures should also provide support, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.19 at $72.16 per cwt, the highest price level since February 22, 1995.
